claim_one_line: L124 -- IS B700's TORSOR THE CMR TORSOR? NO, AND IT WAS NEVER CLOSE. Discharges the debt B942 left when it demoted the values/torsor clause to UNEARNED. NO PREREGISTRATION, DELIBERATELY: the discriminating fact was sitting in B700's own text and surfaced during the mandatory prior-art grep BEFORE any computation, and sealing after seeing the answer would be worse than not sealing -- recorded as an OPEN-AND-SHUT READING so no audit mistakes it for a sealed cell. THE VERDICT IS A CATEGORY DIFFERENCE, not a marginal gap: B700's torsor has structure group Z/2 (order 2, over a QUADRATIC field -- Q(sqrt5) in cell 1, Q(sqrt-7) in cell 2) while CMR's has structure group Gal(K^ab/K), the IDELE CLASS GROUP of K = Q(sqrt-3), which is INFINITE PROFINITE. And B700 does not merely have a Z/2 in one case -- its own summary generalises it: 'at each stage the hearing = a choice among exactly TWO D-dim shadow irreps, with a QUADRATIC character field, swapped simply-transitively by its Galois Z/2'. EVERY B700 TORSOR HAS STRUCTURE GROUP Z/2, and a finite group of order two is not the idele class group of Q(sqrt-3), so the identification B723 relied on is REFUTED, not merely unearned. THE FIELDS ARE MUTUALLY BLIND, computed here rather than cited: (-3|5) = -1 so 5 is INERT in Q(sqrt-3), and (5|3) = -1 so 3 is INERT in Q(sqrt5) -- the banked B857 fact re-derived -- so B700's torsor lives over a field the CMR system's field cannot see, and vice versa; there is no near-miss to rescue. THE CONVERGENCE, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: B723's observer construction had TWO clauses and BOTH have now been corrected IN THE SAME DIRECTION -- chirality, which B723 placed in Gal(K^ab/K), actually lives in Gal(K/Q), order 2 (B942); and values, which B723 also placed in Gal(K^ab/K), actually live in a quadratic Galois Z/2 (B700, this arc). BOTH CLAUSES LAND ON A Z/2 OVER A QUADRATIC FIELD; NEITHER LANDS ON THE INFINITE PROFINITE GROUP B723 ASSIGNED THEM TO. The construction was not wrong in KIND -- it was SYSTEMATICALLY ONE LEVEL TOO HIGH, in both clauses, in the same way. That is a more useful diagnosis than two unrelated errors: right object, wrong level, for the third time in this corpus and now with the pattern named across two clauses at once. WHAT THIS SETTLES: the values clause is not supported by the CMR identification and that identification is dead; L124 CLOSED, negative. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: whether values are a torsor phenomenon AT ALL -- B700 establishes that they ARE, concretely, with its own base-rate gate passed (it checked that 'the value lives in Q(sqrt5) so the group is Z/2' is TRIVIAL and does not count, and verified exactly two irreps, character field exactly Q(sqrt5), and simple transitivity with no fixed point) -- so the values clause is NOT rehabilitated here but is no longer floating: it has a concrete, banked, SMALL torsor of its own, and what was wrong was gluing it to CMR. B723's correction banner should note that BOTH clauses were misplaced, not only chirality. LIMITS: no prereg (see above); 'Gal(K^ab/K) is infinite' is standard class field theory cited not re-derived; and this refutes an IDENTIFICATION, not B700 (which stands entirely) and not B723's motivation -- B723's structure, that a measurement is a choice of fiber functor with Galois ambiguity, SURVIVES, and only its assignment of that ambiguity to the wrong Galois group dies.
